claims.text: The baseline phosphorus-containing HEA/CCA has limited glass-forming ability.
The baseline alloy has moderate thermal stability in its amorphous state.
The baseline alloy tends to crystallize under conventional cooling rates.
The proposed intervention is to increase phosphorus by approximately 2–5 atomic percent relative to the baseline composition.
Rapid solidification conditions can produce amorphous structures in the targeted alloy system.
A moderate phosphorus increase will produce a more homogeneous distribution of isolated phosphorus atoms.
A homogeneous distribution of isolated phosphorus atoms will increase local chemical disorder.
The phosphorus-induced structural state will frustrate long-range atomic ordering.
Additional phosphorus will increase local chemical ordering.
Additional phosphorus will reduce atomic mobility.
Reduced atomic mobility will frustrate nucleation of crystalline phases.
The proposed mechanism will increase the crystallization-onset temperature.
The phosphorus-enriched alloy will require a lower critical cooling rate for glass formation than the baseline alloy.
The phosphorus-enriched alloy will form a fully amorphous structure more readily than the baseline alloy.
Increasing phosphorus beyond an optimal range may cause phase segregation or formation of brittle phosphide phases.
Segregated or brittle phosphide phases may impair amorphous-phase formation or stability.
The effect of phosphorus enrichment may depend on the principal-element mixture and processing conditions.

contradictions.description: The mediator invokes increased local chemical disorder, whereas the mechanism invokes increased local chemical ordering. These can coexist at different length scales, but the hypothesis does not distinguish those scales or reconcile the two descriptions.

The mechanism says the intervention raises the cooling-rate threshold for crystallization, while the predicted outcome says it lowers the critical cooling rate required for glass formation. Under the usual critical-cooling-rate definition these formulations point in opposite directions, unless distinct thresholds are intended.
